articles.title: Cowboys Get Good News on Injured Starter
articles.summary: The Dallas Cowboys could get some good injury news coming in this week if Cobie Durant can make it back for Week 7. The post Cowboys Get Good News on Injured...
articles.body:
It has not been difficult in recent weeks to batter the Dallas Cowboys' defense, either with sharp-witted barbs on social media, or on an actual NFL field with 11 even half-decent offensive players. It's not been a difficult group to push around, ranked 30th in the league in points allowed after Sunday night's 23-13 loss to the Packers in Green Bay, and rated No. 30 among NFL defenses by Pro Football Focus. But in finding fault with this unit, it is worth remembering that much of the back line–including starting corner Cobie Durant, starting safety Jalen Thompson and his backup, PJ Locke–has been lodged on the injured reserve for much of the season so far.

But there is some hope, as we move forward in the season, that we'll start to see some of those players return. That does not mean the Cowboys defense necessarily would be vastly improved. It should, though, set the group up to start mending its ways after a brutal start.

Cowboys Could Have a Decision on Cobie Durant

Locke and Thompson are not due back this week, but could return for Week 8 when their injured reserve time runs up. But there was good news out at The Star when coach Brian Schottenheimer met with reporters in the wake of the Packers loss. Durant, who has been out with a hamstring injury for four weeks, could be back on Monday night for the Cowboys' game against the Eagles.

Said Schottenheimer: "Trending up. Getting him moving a little bit these next couple of days. But he is trending to play."

Schottenheimer added that DeMarvion Overshown could return this week, which would be big because Dee Winters will be out with an Achilles tendon injury.

Getting Durant back would be big, though it could force a tough choice for the Cowboys, who have brought in Joey Porter Jr. to be a starting corner on one boundary while Durant has been out. Durant would be an upgrade over struggling All-Pro DaRon Bland on the other boundary, but will the Cowboys have the stomach to bench their $90 million corner for Durant? That remains to be seen.

articles.title: Dan Quinn Explains 4th Down Confusion After Viral Video During Commanders' Loss to 49ers
articles.summary: During the second quarter of Monday night's contest between the Washington Commanders and San Francisco 49ers, Commanders head coach Dan Quinn appeared to be confused about what down it was.
articles.body:
During the second quarter of Monday night's contest between the Washington Commanders and San Francisco 49ers, Commanders head coach Dan Quinn appeared to be confused about what down it was.

Instead of kicking the field goal in 49ers' territory while trailing 13-3, the Commanders went for it and turned it over on downs. Cameras showed Quinn appearing confused , which led some to believe he didn't know it was fourth down.

After the game, he explained that wasn't the case.

"Definitely knew it was fourth down," he told reporters. "We were going for it... We knew we had to go for some fourth downs to be bold in the game. I didn't think it was going to be a 17-14 game; I thought it was probably gonna be a 28-30 game."

The Commanders went on to lose the game 23-17, so it's hard to say whether it would have made a difference if Washington took the field goal.

Regardless, the Commanders are now 1-4-1, and their playoff hopes are dwindling quickly. Quinn is entering hot-seat territory and can't afford to make any big mistakes moving forward.

articles.title: 49ers sputter in second half after Mike Evans' injury but hold on to beat Commanders to improve to 6-0
articles.summary: The 49ers had a big lead, but the Commanders got back in the game.
articles.body: At some point, the San Francisco 49ers' injuries might bring them down. It almost happened in the second half on Monday night. For now, San Francisco's perfect season rolls on. The 49ers raced out to a 20-point lead and it looked like they would cruise to an easy win over the Washington Commanders. But San Francisco's offense stalled with No. 1 receiver Mike Evans sidelined with an Achilles injury he suffered late in the first half, allowing the Commanders to get back in the game. The Niners' defense, which has been a big surprise all season, came up with two big stops in the final two minutes to seal the 23-17 win. The 49ers improved to 6-0 to start the season. Treylon Burks couldn't haul in a fourth-down pass at the goal line as safety Malik Mustapha, who made a huge hit on a run the previous play, slammed him to the ground. Brock Purdy played well in the first half, as he has all season, but he needs some help. The 49ers are depleted at receiver and it showed in the second half. That allowed the Commanders to get back in it. Washington hurt themselves, particularly with a facemask penalty that negated a touchdown with a little more than four minutes remaining. Jeremy McNichols had a TD here that was wiped away from Chris Paul’s facemask penalty Heartbreaking pic.twitter.com/bvk5eSwiYt— brandon (@JayDanielsMVP) October 20, 2026 The 49ers look like the best team in football about one-third through the season. It has been a great start, but the injuries are becoming a real concern. The Niners have been the unluckiest team when it comes to injuries for a few seasons, and the bad fortune hasn't stopped. Mike Evans injured in first halfIt wouldn't be a 49ers game without a key injury. Evans, who came into the game with injuries to his ribs and Achilles tendon, left Monday night's game due to the Achilles. He stayed down after a catch late in the second quarter and went straight to the locker room with athletic trainers. He was ruled out of the game by the team.The 49ers are getting desperately thin at receiver and the injury to Evans, who has made an immediate impact on San Francisco's offense, would be a big blow if he has to miss time. Head coach Kyle Shanahan said after the game that he didn’t expect the injury to be long-term.Still, it's still a lingering issue for a 33-year-old receiver. And a glimpse at the 49ers’ offense without Evans wasn't pretty.The 49ers slowed down on offense in the second half without Evans and the Commanders got back in the game. Jayden Daniels hit Rachaad White on a touchdown pass with 9:22 left and suddenly Washington had cut San Francisco's lead to 23-17. San Francisco had led 23-3 late in the third quarter. The Commanders forced a quick punt after that and had the ball with a chance to take the lead with 7:46 to go. It looked like an easy night for the 49ers, but Washington was putting San Francisco's perfect record in jeopardy. Second half tightens upOnce Washington started getting momentum, the Commanders were hard to stop. Daniels hadn't had a great night, including strangely throwing the ball away on a fourth down in the first half, but he helped get his team back in the game. He did so without top receiver Terry McLaurin, who was lost in the first half when he was carted off due to a knee injury. The Commanders seemingly took the lead with a little more than four minutes left on a Jeremy McNichols touchdown run, but there was a facemask penalty on Washington guard Chris Paul that negated the score. The 49ers had a big penalty of their own later, when a fourth-down sack was wiped off the board due to an illegal contact penalty that gave Washington a first down. San Francisco came up with the plays it needed, with Mustapha having two big hits on third and fourth down. Washington wasn't finished. It forced a three-and-out and got the ball back with less than a minute to go, but no timeouts. A fair catch interference call helped with field position. The Commanders were running out of time but a 17-yard catch by rookie receiver Antonio Williams got the ball to San Francisco's 28-yard line. But an intentional grounding penalty on Daniels was a crushing blow, especially since there was a 10-second runoff, leaving only six seconds on the clock. A sack on the final play sealed the win.The 49ers survived a scare. Even a great season isn't always going to pretty. And it looks like it could be a memorable year for the 49ers. The injury issues might be the biggest threat to stopping them.
